task: Testbed run that decides PR #1008's own timing mark (vLLM 0792 + sparknet 0001) in candidate-55 without #978, tp4-ring dgx1..dgx4

how_the_pr_bench_works.how_it_ran: Its own single-process job, not against a serving cluster and not multi-rank: on sp3 (one GB10, nothing serving), `docker run --rm --gpus all --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --ulimit memlock=-1` of spark-ds41f:1107 with the PR's changed vLLM files and the prepared sparknet tree mounted, once per 'boot' (two fresh containers): sparknet unittest discover (97 OK), then pytest of the two test files (14 passed), then `bench_roce_core_affinity.py --boot-label bootN --warmup-steps 60 --bench-steps 500 --output ...`.
how_the_pr_bench_works.what_it_measures: A C harness compiled at run time (gcc) stands in for rank 0: a 'sparknet-proxy' pthread spins on a doorbell and does the TP3 one-shot bf16 sum (3 x 3584 elements = 7168 B, 32-slot ring); the calling thread plays the worker main thread, rings 116 doorbells a step and spins for each completion. Per collective: doorbell-to-done latency, proxy wake (doorbell to proxy seeing it) and doorbell to proxy done ('arrival skew'); per step: the 116 collectives' wall time; RUSAGE_THREAD nivcsw of the proxy and the worker. World size 3, no network, no peers, no sparknet code, no serving vLLM; the only image code used is vllm.utils.cpu_affinity.partition_cpu_affinity (the plan) and torch touching CUDA once. 500 steps at ~0.08 ms is ~40 ms of measurement per regime.
how_the_pr_bench_works.how_it_applies_rank0_api_load: Nine synthetic pthreads, each cycling a 256 KiB xorshift working set: 4 'APIServer-Tok' (850 us busy, 150 us asleep), 1 'EngineCore' (700/150), 4 'worker-aux' (600/200), about 7.2 cores of demand, pinned per regime.

regimes.unpinned_0_19: proxy, worker and all load on 10-14 (A725 efficiency cores)
regimes.shared_big_5_9_15_19: proxy, worker and all load on 15-19 only: five X925 cores, not the base's ten-core 5-9,15-19 pool despite the name, so ~9 cores of demand on 5
regimes.partitioned_fast_affinity: the plan for {5-9,15-19}: proxy 19, worker main 18, engine load 17, API load 15-16, aux load 5-9

how_the_pr_bench_works.consequence: The three regimes are hard-coded and compared inside one process, so the result does not depend on the image beyond the plan: on candidate-54 it does not even import (no vllm.utils.cpu_affinity), and on any image with the module it prints the same comparison. It cannot judge an arm. The PR's boot-to-boot swing (shared step p99 0.939 vs 0.085 ms) is one preemption in a ~40 ms sample.

arms.notes: cite no tree hash at all; bin/spark doctor passes on both

the_run.deviation_from_the_brief: The arms are the named profiles plus SPARKNET_ROCE_TRACE=1, not the bare files. sparknet's own per-op trace is the only per-collective timing on the serving path; without it a live arm yields only client chunk gaps (ms) and thread placement, which cannot resolve a 116-collective step (~1-3 ms). Tracing selects sparknet's separately compiled traced kernel and adds a few GPU stores per op, identically in both arms (sparknet's trace.py is the same in candidate-54's tree 8cc28a5c and candidate-55's dab8c457; the bench checks the image's layout before it measures). If the owner wants untraced arms, the bench cannot produce the per-step numbers; drop the overlays and the run reduces to placement + chunk gaps, as the screen's check already gave.

bench_check_1008_bench.py.load: the same in every arm: 16 closed-loop chat streams (check_1008_affinity.py's prompts, temperature 0, thinking off, max_tokens 512) plus 2 loops of /tokenize on one fixed ~118 KB text, against rank 0's API server. The client pins itself to dgx1's CPUs outside the container cpuset (0-4,10-14). The /tokenize part is an addition over the screen's affinity check, to load rank 0's tokenizer as the PR's 'APIServer-Tok' threads did; --tokenize-clients 0 removes it
bench_check_1008_bench.py.window: after 15 s warm-up, rank 0's newest traced sequence opens it; it closes after 60 s or 60,000 sequences (the trace keeps 65,536 records a rank; polled every 2 s); every rank's trace is copied at once to the node's /tmp, then to results/private/lab/candidate-55-mark-1008-tp4/traces-<label>/ on dgx1, verified by size, and the live file is removed from /dev/shm (as scripts/collect_node_traces.py does)
bench_check_1008_bench.py.decisive_number: ring_step_116_collectives_ms: for each traced all-reduce, the slowest rank's kernel time (start to end on its own GPU %globaltimer: stage, wait for every peer's payload, reduce; no cross-node clock), summed over 116 consecutive all-reduces (the decode step's roce_all_reduce count); p99 and mean, PR's percentile method
bench_check_1008_bench.py.why_the_ring_not_rank0: rank 0's own kernel completes on its peers' payloads, so a stalled rank-0 proxy shows on its peers' waits, not on rank 0's own op time. The synthetic check confirms it: 60 rank-0 proxy stalls of 800 us moved the ring step p99 from 1.29 to 2.70 ms and left rank 0's own step p99 at 1.23 ms
bench_check_1008_bench.py.supporting: each rank's own op and step statistics; each rank's proxy wake as excess over its running 1,024-op median (CPU-GPU offset and drift cancel) and counts over 10/100/1000 us; proxy post time; involuntary/voluntary context switches and CPU seconds over the window of every rank's sparknet-proxy and worker main thread (the PR's nivcsw) and the head's engine core and API server; placement and 'partitioned' as check_1008_affinity.py defines it; client chunk gaps and request/tokenize counts
bench_check_1008_bench.py.fails_the_arm_when: the endpoint, a node probe, a trace or a copy fails; the image's trace layout differs; fewer than 11,600 ring ops; any failed request. A failed extra does not stop the job; the verdict marks the run invalid

reading_the_verdict.command: on dgx1 after the run: python3 experiments/2026-10-26-spark-ds41f-candidate/candidate-55/check_1008_bench.py verdict candidate-55-mark-1008-tp4
reading_the_verdict.interval_method: candidates 49-53's rule (as pr-988's result.json): each arm has two boots (candidate-54 and candidate-54-again; candidate-55-no978 and -again). 'lower beyond the interval' = the candidate's higher boot is below the base's lower boot; 'worse/higher' = the candidate's lower boot is above the base's higher boot; otherwise 'same'. The script also prints each arm's repeat margin |boot1 - boot2| and all four base x candidate pairings in percent.
decides: ring_step_116_collectives_ms.p99: must be 'lower' (max of the two candidate boots < min of the two candidate-54 boots)
ring_step_116_collectives_ms.mean: must not be 'higher' (min of the candidate boots not above max of the candidate-54 boots)
validity: all four summaries passed; partitioned false on both candidate-54 boots and true on both candidate-55 boots
reading_the_verdict.context_not_deciding: rank-0 step and op rows, proxy wake excess p99/max and nivcsw (mechanism: should drop on candidate-55 if the partition is what helps), client chunk-gap p99/mean under the load (the 'not worse' side of the trade: rank 0's API server is confined to 15-16 on candidate-55), the kernel job's tests (must pass in both containers) and the PR's in-process numbers (recorded as it ran, not an arm comparison). The mark's tp4-ring part (placement on every rank, screen closed loop, time to ready) is already met on main (receipts/tp4-ring-no978).

validation_on_sp8_cpu_only.kernel-local --dry-run of both bundles: docker command as expected: seccomp unconfined, memlock, the two scripts, dgx4's prepared sparknet tree, the 8 no978 overlay files, workdir vllm

validation_on_sp8_cpu_only.trace layout probe: the bench's layout equals trace.py in both candidate-54's (8cc28a5c) and candidate-55's (dab8c457) sparknet trees
validation_on_sp8_cpu_only.host probe: fake docker top + fake live and stale trace files: live/stale told apart by creation time vs owner start (in-container pids repeat across boots: sp8's /dev/shm already holds old r3-p77..p80 traces), roles from thread names, copy byte-identical

It caught one bug (a shared staging directory), fixed
validation_on_sp8_cpu_only.verdict: on four fake summaries: meets-mark with the interval rule and the placement check

risks: Tracing is untested on this exact stack (prior traced arms: r6m, r6n, older sparknet). If a traced boot fails the lab rolls back and the job stops at that arm; the bench then has nothing to read.

Under the real 16-stream load the base's 10-core pool may rarely preempt the proxy; then the ring p99 reads 'same' and #1008 misses its timing mark on the serving path. That is a valid answer, not a bench fault.
The window holds about 450-520 steps (~900-1,200 all-reduces a second at c16); a p99 over that is its 5th-6th largest step, the same order as the PR's 500.

check_1008_bench.py removes each arm's live trace file from /dev/shm via docker exec rm after copying it; a failed arm can leave one 16 MiB file per rank, removable with `docker exec spark-ds41f rm -f /dev/shm/sparknet-trace-r*` before the next boot or `sudo rm` after.
